scope: Not part of the Western Cape Sprint 5 pattern test. These pins do not feed its predictions, scoring, thresholds or the arrest-gap comparison (tools/checked_signals.py: pattern_test_pins). Collection window: incidents 1-22 Oct 2026. Five other Mpumalanga candidates from the same pass wait on owner decisions and are not in this file.
rules: Standalone signals: no case, entity or map-line links. Incident date kept apart from report date. Pin = the place the source gives; 'approx.' in the title when only a street, suburb, area, village or town is known. Sources that reuse one report or one police statement are not independent corroboration. Being near another pin is not a link. Victims are named when the reports name them (owner decision of 23 Oct 2026); suspects are not named. A gunman who killed himself is not counted as a killing; his death is a note on the killing (owner decision of 23 Oct 2026). Estimated map points (pins D and E): where the place could not be put on a map, the pin is the SAPS station point of the police precinct for that area, used only as a reference; the title says 'map point estimated', the drawer location note starts 'ESTIMATED MAP POINT', and the precision is 'precinct' with an uncertainty equal to the farthest edge of that precinct from the station. Pin C: police are a party (police_party in fact-bases.json). Every fact-base quote matched word for word against the saved source text.
review_status: Approved by the owner on 23 Oct 2026 (voice call, 'Yes'); one explicit version-1 approval record per pin in docs/approvals/pins (reference mpumalanga-approval-2026-10-23).

owner_decisions.decision: Approved for publication as prepared: Siyabuswa, Lillydale Trust, Masoyi, Thusi Village and Amersfoort, with approximate or estimated map points and the police-involved flag on Masoyi. Owner's word: "Yes".

Where a place cannot be mapped, use a clearly labelled police-station estimate (said for Nhlazatshe, MNS, Coronation and Schoemanskloof; applied here to Thusi Village and the Amersfoort farm, the review note's station-estimate option).
Lillydale, Amersfoort and Nhlazatshe: the death count excludes the gunman who killed himself; his death is added as a note on the killing.
If victims are named in the reports, their names go in the findings (Siyabuswa: William Malapane; Lillydale: Marvel Khosa and Ayanda Khosa). Suspects are not named.

signals.title: Siyabuswa (town only, approx.): William Malapane, 44, stabbed at home; wife arrested, 4 Oct
signals.content: Police say officers responding to a complaint at a couple's home in Siyabuswa found William Malapane, 44, with stab wounds to his upper body; he was declared dead at the scene at about 02:00. It is alleged the couple argued before his wife, 40, stabbed him with a sharp object (police spokesperson Colonel Mavela Masondo, via Middelburg Observer). She was arrested on 4 October, charged with murder and denied bail in the Mdutjana Magistrate's Court on 14 October. The victim is named as reported, by the owner's decision of 23 October; the suspect is not named here. One report, resting on police: Middelburg Observer, 19 October. The date is read from the arrest date; the report does not state the date of death. The pin is approximate (town level).

signals.title: Lillydale Trust, Calcutta police area (approx.): Marvel and Ayanda Khosa, mother and daughter, shot dead; gunman then shot himself, 8 Oct
signals.content: Police say a family meeting to resolve domestic issues in Lillydale Trust ended in a shooting at about 16:00 on Thursday 8 October. A man allegedly took a licensed firearm from his vehicle and shot two women, Marvel Khosa and her daughter Ayanda Khosa, who were rushed to a nearby medical facility and declared dead there (police spokesperson Colonel Mavela Masondo, via Lowvelder). This pin counts those two killings. Note: the gunman then allegedly turned the gun on himself and was found dead at the scene; his death is recorded here as a note, not counted as a killing. Calcutta police opened two murder dockets and an inquest docket. The victims are named as reported, by the owner's decision of 23 October; the gunman is not named here. One report, resting on police: Lowvelder, 10 October. The pin is approximate (village level).

signals.title: Bhekiswayo Trust, Masoyi (area only, approx.): man, 30, dies after shoot-out with police; police are a party, 20 Oct
signals.content: Police say a 30-year-old Bhekiswayo Trust man attacked his 73-year-old father with a blunt object, damaged his father's safe and went to a local tavern with a firearm. Officers found he had locked himself inside his parental home; they went in through a window, he fired at an officer and wounded him, and police returned fire, hitting him in the lower body. He later died at a medical facility on or after Tuesday 20 October; his father survived (SAPS spokesperson Colonel Mavela Masondo, via Lowvelder; SAPS Mpumalanga statement of 21 October). Cases of attempted murder (the father and the officer), possession of an unlicensed firearm and an inquest were opened; SAPS and IPID are investigating. Police are a party to this death, and police are the only source: there is no independent account. He is not named in the reports. One report: Lowvelder, 22 October. The pin is approximate (area level).

signals.title: Thusi Village, Ermelo police area (map point estimated): woman, 27, found dead after alleged assault; man, 31, charged with murder, 2 Oct
signals.content: Police say they received a complaint that a woman was being assaulted by her male friend in Thusi Village; officers found her unconscious on the ground and paramedics declared her dead at the scene. A 31-year-old man still in the area was arrested on 2 October and charged with murder (police spokesperson Colonel Mavela Masondo, via Highvelder News). He appeared in the Ermelo Magistrate's Court and the case was postponed to 12 October for plea. The family is waiting for post-mortem results to confirm the cause of death. She is not named in the report. One report, resting on police: Highvelder News, 5 October. MAP POINT ESTIMATED: Thusi Village could not be placed on a map, so the pin sits on the Ermelo police station, in the area that dealt with the case. It is not the scene; the village may be up to about 44 km away.

signals.title: Farm near Amersfoort (map point estimated): farm worker, about 50, shot dead in hostage incident; gunman then shot himself, 10 Oct
signals.content: Police say they were called to a hostage situation on a farm near Amersfoort at about 06:00 on Saturday 10 October and found three people who had escaped. A 55-year-old armed man allegedly held farm workers hostage, then shot one, aged about 50, dead and shot another, aged about 53, who survived and was airlifted to hospital (police spokesperson Brigadier Donald Mdhluli, via The Citizen). This pin counts that one killing. Note: while police negotiators were talking to him, the gunman reportedly shot himself and was certified dead at the scene; his death is recorded here as a note, not counted as a killing. A 9mm pistol was found. Cases of murder, attempted murder and kidnapping were opened. No one is named in the report. One report, resting on police: The Citizen, 10 October. MAP POINT ESTIMATED: the farm is not named, so the pin sits on the Amersfoort police station. It is not the scene; the farm may be up to about 43 km away.
